page_title: Implementing an A+ Conformant Promise Library in JavaScript the TDD Way

summary.title: Implementing an A+ Conformant Promise Library in JavaScript the TDD Way
summary.one_liner: You learn how Promises/A+ work internally by building a conformant promise class in JavaScript, one Jest test at a time.
keywords: how do promises work under the hood
takeaways: A promise is a state machine (PENDING, FULFILLED, REJECTED) that can transition only once.
The then method queues handlers while pending and returns a new promise whose state depends on the handler's result or error.
Handlers returning promises or thenables must be unwrapped, and handlers must run after the event loop to be consistent.
Compliance edge cases include invalid handlers, self-resolution (TypeError), and rejecting with a promise, all verified against the A+ compliance suite (872 tests passing).
summary.summary: The author builds a Promises/A+ conformant promise class in JavaScript using a test-driven workflow with Jest. Each section introduces a spec requirement, shows the tests first, then the implementation: the executor and state transitions, the then method with handler queues, promise chaining, adoption of nested promises and thenables, invalid handlers, asynchronous handler execution, and self-resolution errors. The final implementation passed all 872 tests of the A+ compliance suite. The article closes with possible improvements such as a task queue, Promise.all and Promise.race, and performance work.
